hints: Divide $x^4 + 16$ by $x^2 + 4$ using polynomial long division.
State the quadratic quotient $x^2 - 4$ and constant remainder $32$.
walkthrough:
Divide $x^4 + 16$ by $x^2 + 4$ by algebraic division:
1. First quotient term: $\dfrac{x^4}{x^2} = x^2$.
   Multiply and subtract:
   $$(x^4 + 16) - x^2(x^2 + 4) = x^4 + 16 - x^4 - 4x^2 = -4x^2 + 16$$

2. Second quotient term: $\dfrac{-4x^2}{x^2} = -4$.
   Multiply and subtract:
   $$(-4x^2 + 16) - (-4)(x^2 + 4) = -4x^2 + 16 - (-4x^2 - 16) = 16 + 16 = 32$$

State the quotient and remainder:
$$\text{Quotient} = x^2 - 4$$
$$\text{Remainder} = 32$$

hints: Integrate $x^2 - 4$ to $\dfrac{x^3}{3} - 4x$ and $\dfrac{32}{x^2 + 4}$ to $16\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$, then evaluate limits to show $\dfrac{4}{3}(\pi + 4)$.
walkthrough:
Rewrite the integrand using the quotient and remainder from part (a):
$$\int_2^{2\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{x^4 + 16}{x^2 + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_2^{2\sqrt{3}} \left(x^2 - 4 + \dfrac{32}{x^2 + 2^2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = 2\sqrt{3}$:
$$\dfrac{(2\sqrt{3})^3}{3} - 4(2\sqrt{3}) = \dfrac{24\sqrt{3}}{3} - 8\sqrt{3} = 8\sqrt{3} - 8\sqrt{3} = 0$$
$$16\arctan\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 16\arctan(\sqrt{3}) = 16\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{16\pi}{3}$$
$$\text{Upper value} = \dfrac{16\pi}{3}$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 2$:
$$\dfrac{2^3}{3} - 4(2) = \dfrac{8}{3} - 8 = \dfrac{8 - 24}{3} = -\dfrac{16}{3}$$
$$16\arctan\left(\dfrac{2}{2}\right) = 16\arctan(1) = 16\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 4\pi = \dfrac{12\pi}{3}$$
$$\text{Lower value} = -\dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{12\pi}{3}$$

Subtract lower limit value from upper limit value:
$$\text{Integral} = \dfrac{16\pi}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{12\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{16\pi}{3} - \dfrac{12\pi}{3} + \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3} + \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}(\pi + 4)$$
